name: Em dash use
definition: Presence of at least one em dash (U+2014) or ' -- ' standing in for one. Variants: >=2 dashes; spaced ' — '; closed 'word—word'.
exact_matching_method: textlib.detect: emdash_count = count('—') + count(r'\w\s?--\s?\w'); flags emdash_any (>=1), emdash_ge2, emdash_spaced (r'\s—\s'), emdash_closed (r'\w—\w'). Dashes inside quoted '>' paragraphs and code are removed before counting.
possible_false_positives: Autocorrect on phones and word processors; typographers, journalists and many fiction writers; pasted text from other tools; Victorian prose (analyzer baseline 33 of 300 chunks).

name: Contrast frame ('not X but Y')
definition: Negative-parallelism sentence: denies a reading, then states the 'real' one.
exact_matching_method: strict = ports of the analyzer's RHE-NOT-JUST / RHE-ITS-NOT-ABOUT regexes; broad = r'\b(not|isn't|aren't|wasn't|doesn't|don't|didn't|never)\b [^.!?]{2,80}?(,|;|—|--|...)\s*(but|rather|instead|it's|that's|this is|they're)\b'; 'x_not_y' = r'[A-Za-z]+( [A-Za-z]+){0,4}, not (a|an|the|just|only)? [A-Za-z]+'.
possible_false_positives: Ordinary argument ('I did not say X, but Y'); speeches; the broad and x_not_y variants match everyday disagreement.

name: Rhetorical question + short fragment answer
definition: A question sentence immediately followed by an answer of 1-6 words ('Why does it matter? Simple.').
possible_false_positives: Conversational asides ('Honestly? It works.'); teaching and ad copy by humans.

name: Repeated sentence openings
definition: Three or more consecutive sentences beginning with the same word.
exact_matching_method: opening_run_max >= 3 on a lowercase first-word comparison (analyzer uses 4).

name: Three-part construction
definition: Adjective/noun triple ('fast, cheap, and reliable'). Only the adjective-triple form is matched.
possible_false_positives: Any ordinary list of three; very high false-positive risk; noun/clause tricolons are NOT matched (unmeasured).

name: Bullets / numbered lists
definition: Lines starting with -, *, a bullet, or '1.'/'1)'.
possible_false_positives: Technical comments, steps, quotes of lists. HN does not render markdown; bullets are typed.

name: Bold / headings in casual text
definition: Markdown bold (**x**) or heading (# x).
possible_false_positives: HN has no bold or headings, so near-zero by platform. Cannot be tested on this corpus.

name: Generic affirmation / enthusiasm opener
definition: Opening sentence of praise ('Great question', 'You're absolutely right', 'That's a fascinating point').
exact_matching_method: anchored regex at start of text; see textlib R('generic_affirm').
possible_false_positives: Politeness; replies to a direct question.

name: Formulaic transition openers
definition: Sentence-initial 'Furthermore', 'Moreover', 'Additionally', 'Overall', 'Notably' and kin.
exact_matching_method: first words of each sentence vs the analyzer's 14-item list (never however/therefore/but).

name: Uniform sentence rhythm
definition: Low coefficient of variation of sentence lengths over >=8 sentences and >=150 words.
exact_matching_method: not computed as a binary here: almost no comment meets the length floor; reported as applicable-n only.

name: Polish / register mismatch for the context
definition: Writing judged too polished or formal for a casual setting.
exact_matching_method: NOT operationalised: no deterministic definition. Counted only when an accuser names it.

name: Generic metaphor / hyperbole / stock phrase
definition: Any of the analyzer's 9 stock phrases ('plays a crucial role', 'a testament to'...) or hyperbole/stock words (seamless, robust, tapestry, crucial, vital, pivotal...).
possible_false_positives: 'crucial', 'vital', 'robust' are ordinary words in technical prose.

name: Balanced paragraphs
definition: Paragraphs of near-equal length (>=4 paragraphs).

name: Repetitive short fragments (staccato)
definition: Three or more consecutive sentences of at most 6 words.

name: Closing engagement question
definition: Text ends with a reader-directed question ('What do you think?', 'Have you tried...?').
exact_matching_method: last sentence ends '?' and (matches closing markers or contains 'you'/'your').

name: Low information density / vague claims
definition: No digits and no mid-sentence capitalised names in a text of >=80 words (proxy).
possible_false_positives: Opinion and reflective comments are legitimately abstract.

name: Stock vocabulary (e.g. 'delve')
definition: Analyzer stock phrases (includes 'delve into').

name: Unspecified 'tone' / 'voice'
definition: Accuser cites tone, voice, cadence or a feeling with no concrete feature.
exact_matching_method: accuser-named only; not computable from text.

name: Length / verbosity
definition: Accuser says the text is too long or padded.

name: Emoji
definition: Emoji or dingbats.

name: Curly quotes / apostrophes
definition: Typographic ’ “ ” in the text (typed text on desktop is usually straight).
possible_false_positives: iOS and macOS smart punctuation; word processors. Emergent hypothesis, not preregistered.

name: Semicolon
definition: Any semicolon.

name: Hedge-balance phrases
definition: 'on the one hand', 'on the other hand', 'that said', 'with that said'.

name: Listicle scaffolding
definition: 'Here's the thing', 'Here's why', 'The real problem is', 'Let's dive', 'break this down'.

name: Label-colon lines
definition: Lines starting 'Label: text'.

name: Off-topic or non-responsive reply
definition: Accuser says the reply does not address what was asked, restates the parent, or is oddly generic.

name: Marketing / advertisement / SEO / self-help tone
definition: Accuser says the text reads like an ad, SEO content, clickbait or a self-help formula.
exact_matching_method: accuser-named only (fixed regex over free-text cues in registry.other_to_pattern).

name: Specific quoted stock phrase or opener
definition: Accuser quotes a particular phrase as the tell ('the uncomfortable truth', 'in summary').

name: Repetition / duplicated or templated text
definition: Accuser says text repeats itself, duplicates earlier points or follows a template.
